newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt to introduce accrual accounting.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt to introduce accrual accounting.

text.p: The Australian government said on Wednesday it would introduce accrual accounting for its financial transactions, improving the way it budgeted and bringing it into line with state government practices.
Under accrual accounting, actual economic transactions are recorded when they take place, independent of whether the cash related payment is made at that time.
As such, accrual accounting keeps a register of assets and liabilities, including debtors and creditors.
Until now, the government has worked on a cash accounting basis -- recording transactions when a cash payment is made.
Finance Minister John Fahey said the government's decision was consistent with recommendations made in 1995 by a national commission looking at the government's financial framework.

"With the adoption of the accrual framework, the government and its agencies will prepare their budgets, manage their operations and prepare their financial reports on a basis similar to that used by business," Fahey said in a statement.
The accrual framework would be gradually introduced until fully implemented, including an accruals budget and quarterly accrual reports, in the 1999/2000 (July/June) fiscal year.
